articles.content: EXCLUSIVE: Lily James is attached to star in and produce a feature adaptation of Lucy Foley ’s bestselling novel The Hunting Party for Universal Pictures. James will produce and Gala Gordon will co-produce for Parodos Productions. Molly Sims is also producing along with Gaby McCormick for Something Happy Productions. No writer is currently attached. A Sunday Times and New York Times bestseller, The Hunting Party follows a group of old Oxford friends whose holiday reunion at a remote hunting lodge turns deadly when a blizzard leaves them snowbound, and one of them is found murdered. The novel established Foley as a leading voice in commercial thrillers and was shortlisted for Crime & Thriller Book of the Year at the British Book Awards. Not to be confused with the NBC procedural drama of the same name created by J.J. Bailey that aired for two seasons between 2025 and 2026, Foley’s The Hunting Party was published in December 2018. Foley will executive produce. Foley has sold over 12 million copies worldwide and is a New York Times and Sunday Times No. 1 bestselling author. articles.content: The holidays have arrived early, as HBO Max has revealed that its critically acclaimed medical drama, The Pitt , will premiere its third season on January 7, 2027. The news dropped today via the show’s Instagram account, with actors Taylor Dearden, Isa Briones, and Gerran Howell dressed as their characters Mel, Santos, and Whitaker, respectively. The trio is in the locker room, with little reveals shown in their compartments: Santos’ says The Pitt returns on a pink sticky note, and Mel finds a small package that also has a pink sticky note that reads January 7. The Pitt chronicles the urgent challenges U.S. frontline healthcare professionals face through the lens of the fictional Pittsburgh Trauma Medical Center’s emergency department. Offering a real-time format, the series traces, hour by hour, the medical cases and personal crises physicians and nurses must navigate as they reckon with an overabundance of patients and a lack of resources. articles.content: Gerald R. Molen, the Oscar-winning producer behind Steven Spielberg ’s “Schindler’s List,” has died. He was 91. Molen’s death was announced by his great-niece, Rachel Lorraine Pullan, in an Instagram post on Sunday. “This morning my great-uncle, Gerald R. Molen, passed on to join my great-grandma and his dear wife Pat on the other side of the veil. I am so happy for him, and also so very sad,” she wrote. “Uncle Jerry was a man of great moral character and high integrity. articles.content: John Travolta rarely connects with all his characters. articles.content: Danny Boyle has thrown his support behind his “Ink” star Jack O’Connell as the man to battle Robert Pattinson ‘s James Bond in the next 007 movie. articles.title: Gérard Depardieu to Stand Trial for Rape Charges After Failed Appeal
articles.content: French actor Gérard Depardieu will face a criminal rape trial after an appeal from his lawyers failed. According to Reuters , on Thursday the Paris Court of Appeal ruled that a trial would go ahead regarding rape charges that stemmed from accusations made by actress Charlotte Arnould in 2018. She alleged that in August of that year, Depardieu raped her twice at his Paris home. He was indicted in December 2020 and has denied any wrongdoing. Last year, his lawyers appealed the prosecutors’ decision for the case to go to trial. articles.content: Gerald R. Molen, the Oscar-winning producer who teamed with Steven Spielberg on films including Schindler’s List , Jurassic Park and Minority Report , has died. He was 91. A longtime resident of Bigfork, Montana, Molen died Monday, his great-niece Rachel Lorraine Pullan announced . Molen first worked with Spielberg as a unit production manager on The Color Purple (1985), after which the filmmaker offered him his first producing gig, as an associate producer on *batteries not included (1987). Molen’s producing credits outside of Spielberg and Amblin included the best picture winner Rain Man (1988), Days of Thunder (1990), The Other Side of Heaven (2001), Just Like Heaven (2005), The Meg (2018) and Meg 2: The Trench (2023). articles.content: In one of the most sweeping, romantic moments of The Other Bennet Sister , Tom Hayward (Dónal Finn) recites the poem “Composed Upon Westminster Bridge” for Mary Bennet (Ella Bruccoleri), Pride & Prejudice ‘s misfit sibling turned unlikely romantic heroine. The delivery of the poem is wrenching; the scene, in a small rainy garden, idyllic. And yet the scene, adapted by screenwriter Sarah Quintrell from Janice Hadlow’s novel of the same name, was scaled back dramatically from how it reads in the book — taking place against the splendor of the actual Westminster Bridge. We couldn’t film on Westminster Bridge — we just couldn’t afford it,” according to Emmy-winning executive producer Jane Tranter ( Succession ). “We were cramped into this tiny little garden full of rain…to create a scene that just feels so big and so moving and so emotional on very, very little. articles.summary: Franchise producer Nina Jacobson says adapting one book into two movies rubs fans the wrong way: "I think audiences find it cynical."
articles.content: Author Suzanne Collins’ climactic Katniss novel Mockingjay was infamously split into two films, Part 1 and Part 2 . Both are considered a step down from the previous two Hunger Games blockbusters, with lower Rotten Tomatoes critic and audience scores. The uneven Part 1 , in particular, felt like a franchise spinning its wheels. To fans, it all looked like a studio trying to wring more ticket sales from the story. articles.title: Ava DuVernay to Receive London Critics’ Circle Inaugural Laura Mulvey Female Trailblazer Award
articles.summary: The newly created honor, which DuVernay will collect from Mulvey herself at the London Critics' Circle Film Awards, recognizes the most influential women in film working to break the glass ceiling.
articles.content: American filmmaker Ava DuVernay is the first recipient of the London Critics’ Circle’s inaugural Laura Mulvey Female Trailblazer Award. DuVernay, who this year has taken her most recent documentary, 14th , on the festival circuit, will accept the newly created honor from Mulvey herself at the London Critics’ Circle Film Awards ceremony in the British capital on Feb. 7. The Laura Mulvey Female Trailblazer Award is designed to recognize “the most influential women in film, who are working to break the glass ceiling, change the cultural conversation, and be an example of what is possible for future generations,” according to London Critics’ Circle. DuVernay’s 14th — set to release in U.K. cinemas Nov. 27 before dropping on Netflix Dec. 4 — is an exploration of American democracy through the lens of the foundational 14th Amendment, exposing an unfinished battle to define America, now taking on drastic new dimensions. articles.title: TV Ratings: ‘Dancing With the Stars’ Records Another Huge Finale
articles.summary: Early ratings are at a 12-year high among adults 18-49 and even with last year in total viewers.
articles.content: The season 35 finale of Dancing With the Stars capped off a season of big ratings with the show’s best numbers of the fall. Early Nielsen ratings have the finale — which aired live coast to coast, a first for DWTS — averaging 9.2 million viewers, on par with preliminary numbers for last season’s final episode . The season 34 finale ended up at 9.43 million viewers after the addition of Nielsen’s big data component; final same-day numbers for Tuesday’s show will be available after Thanksgiving. The DWTS finale also scored the show’s best rating among adults 18-49 in more than a decade: It’s currently at 2.38 (equivalent to about 3.24 million people in the demographic), subject to adjustments. That’s the highest rating for a Dancing With the Stars episode since the season 19 finale in 2014 — when current host Alfonso Ribeiro won the mirror ball trophy — and the highest mark for a regularly scheduled network entertainment show (i.e., not a special like the Oscars or Grammys) since an episode of The Masked Singer in April 2020. The finale also scored a 15-year high among adults under 35 with a 2.86 rating — an almost unheard-of number for anything outside of live sports in the current broadcast environment. Pending updates for the finale, season 35 of DWTS averaged 7.19 million viewers, up about 11 percent from last year. The show’s 1.59 rating among adults 18-49 is up by almost 20 percent year to year. The latter number ranks first among all network shows this fall, excluding live sports, and leads second-place Survivor (0.86 rating) by a canyon-sized 86 percent margin. Should that hold, it would be the largest gap between a first- and second-place show in the 18-49 demo since the beginning of Nielsen’s electronic measurement in 1991. ABC says viewers cast a record-setting 86 million votes during the finale, up from 72 million for the season 34 closer. DWTS also generated the most social media engagements of any primetime program Tuesday.

articles.title: TV Ratings: NBA Logs Winning Streak in First Month of the Season
articles.summary: Audiences on national media partners NBC/Peacock, ESPN and Prime Video are up by 37 percent year to year.
articles.content: Like a jump shooter who can’t miss, the NBA is on a heater with TV audiences through the first month of its 2026-27 season. National telecasts of league games on NBC/Peacock, ESPN and Prime Video are averaging 2.62 million viewers over the season’s first month, based on Nielsen ratings and Adobe Analytics figures for Peacock’s games. That’s a sizable, 37 percent increase over the same time frame last year — the first in the league’s current media rights deal with NBCUniversal, ESPN and Prime Video. Through last week, every national telecast had topped 1 million viewers, the first time that’s happened since 2023. Related Stories TV TV Ratings: 'Dancing With the Stars' Records Another Huge Finale TV Streaming Ratings: 'Rings of Power,' 'Black Doves' Open Lower After Long Gaps Between Seasons That’s also the highest mark on record for the first month of an NBA season, excluding lockout-delayed starts in 1999 and 2011 (and with the caveat that changes in Nielsen measurement the past few years have tended to benefit live sports). NBC’s six national windows lead the way with an average of 4.5 million viewers (including streaming on Peacock), a 27 percent improvement over last season’s first month.. The network’s opening night game between the defending champion New York Knicks and the Philadelphia 76ers (who acquired LeBron James during the offseason) averaged 7.71 million cross-platform viewers. The first eight games on Prime Video have averaged 2.05 million viewers, and ESPN is at 1.8 million viewers across 13 telecasts. Prime Video has grown by a huge 83 percent year to year, and ESPN’s games are up 13 percent. Prime Video has the youngest audience of the NBA’s three national media partners (the same is true for Prime relative to other NFL broadcasters); its median viewer age is a little under 46. ESPN and NBC (not including Peacock viewers) have a median age of about 53 for NBA games.

She leads a mostly male group of bikers with a passion for vengeance. Zelda makes an ultimatum with Margo Banks as she’s on the hunt for her brother Kyle. What Zelda doesn’t know is that Kyle is dead. It’s later discovered that Zelda’s granddaughter is Elly. articles.title: Gérard Depardieu Loses Appeal, Faces Rape Trial
articles.summary: A Paris appeals court rules the "Cyrano de Bergerac" star will proceed to trial for 2018 allegations from actress Charlotte Arnould The post Gérard Depardieu Loses Appeal, Faces Rape Trial appeared first on TheWrap .
articles.content: A Paris appeals court rules the “Cyrano de Bergerac” star will proceed to trial for 2018 allegations from actress Charlotte Arnould French actor Gérard Depardieu will proceed to a rape trial against actress Charlotte Arnould, a Paris appeals court ruled on Thursday. The court rejected Depardieu’s bid to avoid having his case, revolving around an alleged 2018 rape, thrown out. The case dates back to two separate incidents from August 2018, wherein Arnould, then in her early 20s, alleges Depardieu, then in his late 60s, sexually assaulted her in her home. The Paris appeals court ruled that Depardieu would be tried for the first alleged incident, which occurred on Aug. 7, 2018, while dismissing a second alleged incident, which occurred Aug. 13, 2018. This news comes hot on the heels of Depardieu withdrawing his appeal for a separate sexual assault trial for which he was convicted in May 2025 . Depardieu was found guilty of sexually assaulting two women on the set of his 2021 film, “Les Volets Verts.” He was given an 18-month suspended prison sentence and a fine of roughly $32,350 (including one victim’s medical fees), with his name additionally added to France’s sex offender registry. Depardieu withdrew that appeal on Nov. 16, stating that he used “vulgar, ​sexually suggestive humour” on set and realizes now that “there is a line between cheekiness ⁠and offence,” in a statement provided to Reuters . The French actor apologized by giving “his deepest and ​most sincere apologies to all those who may ​have suffered as a result,” sharing that he decided to withdraw his appeal because he’d “come ​to realize that I belonged to ​a world that no longer exists.” If convicted in his trial against Arnould, Depardieu could face 15 to 20 years in jail. Depardieu could still appeal to the Cour ⁠de Cassation, France’s highest court, his lawyer noted, per NBC News and Reuters .

articles.content: Amid all the sex and murder in “The Hunting Wives” Season 2 — and there is a lot of sex and murder — the riskiest scene suspends itself between the two. Sophie (Brittany Snow), an East Coast liberal out of place in the conservative Texas town of Maple Brook, and Margo (Malin Åkerman), the mysterious local matriarch who can wrap just about anyone around her finely manicured fingertips, are confronted with a fresh dilemma. For spoilers sake, I won’t get into specifics, but the issue is urgent and impacts them both, without being serious enough to warrant what turns out to be their first-thought fix: In the moment, their lethal instinct seems reasonable. Margo already shot a pregnant teenager in the woods, and Sophie committed vehicular homicide against Margo’s brother (which invited suspicions about Sophie’s past, considering its eerie similarities to a deadly “accident” back in Massachusetts).
